title: Bidar Sultanate
capsule: The Bidar Sultanate (Barid Shahi dynasty) emerged in 1492 when Qasim Barid I, formerly a minister of the fragmenting Bahmani Sultanate, established autonomous control over the city of Bidar in the central Deccan of present-day Karnataka. The sultanate was the smallest of the five Deccan Sultanates and played a notably cautious diplomatic role, participating in the coalition that defeated the Vijayanagara Empire at the Battle of Talikota in 1565 under Ali Barid Shah I. Bidar's architectural legacy includes the Barid Shahi tombs, notable for their synthesis of Deccani Islamic and Hindu decorative traditions. The dynasty was extinguished in 1619 when Ibrahim Adil Shah II of the Bijapur Sultanate annexed Bidar.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's territory around Bidar city is consistently described in Persian chronicles and European traveler accounts; precise boundaries with neighboring Deccan sultanates are approximate due to fluctuating frontier agreements.
